checklist.step: Inventory the board/committee structure the ICA and OSFI's Corporate Governance Guideline require
actions: In the board portal open the Governance workspace and list the mandated bodies: full Board, Audit Committee (ss. 337-356 auditor oversight), Conduct Review Committee (s. 204), and the Investment/Risk Committee overseeing ss. 492-495 limits.
For each body confirm an active charter is on file; flag any body with no charter or a charter version older than 12 months.
Cross-check the mandated-body list against the OSFI Corporate Governance Guideline checklist and note any gap.
Send the gap list to the Board Governance Lead for charter drafting.
checklist.done: every ICA/OSFI-mandated body has an identified charter status (current, stale, or missing) recorded in the board portal.

checklist.step: Draft or refresh each committee charter against the ICA sections it implements
actions: For the Investment/Risk Committee, write the mandate to include quarterly review of compliance with the Investment Limits (Insurance Companies) Regulations (aggregate real property, equity and commercial-loan limits under ss. 492-495).
For the Board itself, write in the s. 515(1) duty to review capital and liquidity adequacy at each regular meeting.
For any foreign-branch operation, add the s. 608 margin-of-assets oversight duty to the relevant committee's mandate.
Route the draft to General Counsel for legal sufficiency review before it goes to the Board.
checklist.done: each charter draft names the ICA section it discharges and has passed General Counsel's legal-sufficiency review.

checklist.step: Confirm director and committee composition against ICA eligibility rules
actions: Pull the current director roster from the board portal and check Canadian-residency and independence counts against the ICA composition requirements.
Confirm the Conduct Review Committee and Audit Committee are composed entirely of directors who are not officers or employees of the company.
Where a vacancy or non-compliant composition is found, notify the Nominating Committee Chair the same week.
Record the composition check result and date on the governance calendar.
checklist.done: the current composition of every mandated committee is confirmed against ICA rules or a named vacancy is escalated.

checklist.step: Schedule the mandated meeting cadence in the board portal
actions: In the board portal calendar, create the year's recurring meetings for the Board and each committee at the cadence set in its charter (quarterly minimum for the Investment Committee).
Attach the charter-mandated quorum requirement to each meeting invite.
Send calendar holds to all directors and named management attendees at least 30 days ahead of the year's first meeting.
Set a T-5 business day reminder for pack distribution ahead of each meeting.
checklist.done: the full year's mandated meetings are on the board portal calendar with quorum requirements and reminders attached.

checklist.step: Prepare and distribute the meeting pack for each session
actions: Assemble the agenda, prior minutes, and the relevant committee report (Investment Committee limits monitoring report, capital/liquidity dashboard for s. 515(1), or branch margin-of-assets report for s. 608) into the board portal pack.
Request the underlying report from the Chief Risk Officer (limits monitoring) or CFO (capital/liquidity dashboard) at least 10 business days before the meeting.
Publish the pack in the board portal and confirm every named attendee has acknowledged receipt.
Log any late report as a pack-completeness exception.
checklist.done: the pack, including the ICA-relevant oversight report, is published in the board portal and acknowledged by attendees before the meeting.

checklist.step: Take and circulate minutes, including the ICA-oversight discussion
actions: Record attendance, quorum confirmation, and the substance of any ss. 492-495 limits discussion, s. 515(1) capital/liquidity review, or s. 608 branch review on the agenda item.
Note any limit breach, capital shortfall risk, or margin-of-assets concern raised and the action assigned.
Circulate draft minutes to attendees within 5 business days of the meeting for factual accuracy comment.
File the approved minutes in the board portal against the meeting record.
checklist.done: approved minutes documenting the ICA-oversight discussion and any assigned actions are filed in the board portal.

checklist.step: Verify the Investment Committee reviewed the ss. 492-495 limits report each cycle
actions: Confirm the quarterly limits monitoring report (real property, equity, commercial loan ratios to total assets) was tabled and discussed at the Investment Committee.
Check that any limit approaching or exceeding the Investment Limits Regulations threshold has a documented committee response.
Sign the report as reviewed and file it with the meeting minutes.
checklist.done: each Investment Committee cycle shows a signed, discussed limits report with any threshold issue actioned.

checklist.step: Confirm the Board's s. 515(1) capital/liquidity adequacy review occurred
actions: Check the Board agenda for the regular capital/liquidity adequacy item and confirm the CFO's dashboard was presented.
Verify the minutes record the Board's conclusion on adequacy and any capital action directed.
Where the item was deferred, reschedule it into the next meeting within 30 days and flag the gap.
checklist.done: every regular Board meeting shows a minuted capital/liquidity adequacy review or a logged, rescheduled deferral.

checklist.step: Confirm branch margin-of-assets oversight under s. 608 where applicable
actions: For any Canadian branch of a foreign company in scope, confirm the relevant committee reviewed the margin-of-assets calculation against s. 608 at least annually.
Check the minutes name the calculated margin and confirm it meets the prescribed requirement.
Escalate to the Chief Agent for the branch if the margin is close to or below the required level.
checklist.done: the branch margin-of-assets review is minuted annually with the calculated margin on record, or escalated if deficient.

checklist.step: Obtain Board approval on any charter amendment
actions: Table the redlined charter as a Board resolution item with the reason for amendment stated.
Record the Board vote and effective date of the amended charter in the board portal.
Publish the new charter version and archive the superseded version with its retirement date.
checklist.done: every charter amendment carries a dated Board approval resolution and a version history in the board portal.

checklist.step: File the OSFI notification of director/committee-membership changes
actions: On any new director appointment, resignation, or committee reassignment, complete OSFI's Changes in Corporate Information return with the effective date and biography/fit-and-proper attestation.
Submit the return within the prescribed notification period after the change takes effect.
File the submission confirmation in the governance record for that director.
checklist.done: every director/committee change has a timely OSFI notification on file with a submission confirmation.

checklist.step: Maintain the governance calendar and flag missed meetings
actions: Reconcile the year-to-date meeting log against the charter-mandated cadence for each body.
Flag any body that has fallen behind its required cadence and schedule a make-up session within 30 days.
Report cadence status to the Board Governance Lead monthly.
checklist.done: the governance calendar shows every mandated body on or ahead of its charter cadence, with make-up sessions scheduled where behind.

checklist.step: Log quorum failures or charter lapses as exceptions
actions: Raise a GRC platform issue for any meeting that failed quorum or any charter that lapsed past its review date.
Assign a root cause (director vacancy, scheduling conflict, missed renewal) and a named owner.
Set a remediation date and link the resolving action (make-up meeting, charter re-approval) when closed.
checklist.done: every quorum failure or charter lapse has a GRC issue with root cause, owner and remediation date.

checklist.step: Obtain General Counsel sign-off on remediation before the committee reconvenes
actions: Review the remediation action against the logged exception and confirm it cures the composition, quorum or charter gap.
Sign and date the remediation record before the affected committee's next scheduled meeting.
Notify the Corporate Secretary to close the GRC issue.
checklist.done: no remediation is closed, and no affected committee reconvenes, without General Counsel's dated sign-off.

checklist.step: Retain charters, minutes and attendance evidence
actions: Move the finalized charter, minutes and attendance register into the compliance evidence repository under the meeting date and body name.
Apply the 7-year retention label, and mark the currently-in-force charter as permanent retention.
Confirm the repository index is searchable by committee name and meeting date.
checklist.done: the governance record for the period is filed, retention-labelled, and searchable in the evidence repository.

testing.step: Build the population of Board/committee meetings and charter versions in the period
actions: Extract from the board portal every Board and committee meeting held, and every charter version approved, in the test quarter.
Reconcile the extract count to the governance calendar's planned cadence for the period.
Resolve any discrepancy (extra, missing or rescheduled meetings) before sampling.
testing.done: the population is reconciled to the governance calendar and signed as complete.

testing.step: Reconcile each meeting to a quorum record and each committee to a current charter
actions: Match every meeting to its attendance register and confirm quorum as defined in the applicable charter.
Match every committee to a charter version dated within the prior 12 months.
List unmatched meetings or stale charters as automatic exceptions.
testing.done: every meeting is matched to a quorum record and a current charter, or listed as an exception.

testing.step: Select the sample and document the selection method
actions: Take 100% of Investment Committee meetings (limits oversight is the highest-risk item).
Take a random sample of 8 additional Board/committee meetings, seeded and reproducible.
Record the seed, population size and selection date in the workpaper.
testing.done: the sample is drawn, reproducible, and covers every Investment Committee meeting in the period.

testing.step: Re-perform the composition check on the sample
actions: For each sampled meeting, independently re-check director residency and independence counts against the ICA composition rules as of the meeting date.
Compare the result to the composition record maintained by the Corporate Secretary; log any difference as an exception.
Capture the roster snapshot used into the workpaper.
testing.done: each sampled meeting has an independently re-performed composition result recorded and reconciled.

testing.step: Verify the ss. 492-495 limits report was reviewed at each sampled Investment Committee meeting
actions: Open the minutes and the attached limits monitoring report for each sampled Investment Committee meeting.
Recompute the real property, equity and commercial-loan ratios to total assets from the underlying investment ledger and compare to the report presented.
Flag any material variance between the recomputed ratio and the reported ratio as an exception.
testing.done: the limits report reviewed at each sampled meeting is independently recomputed and reconciles within tolerance.

testing.step: Verify the s. 515(1) capital/liquidity adequacy review occurred as minuted
actions: Confirm the CFO's capital/liquidity dashboard referenced in the minutes exists and matches the figures in the OSFI capital return for the same period.
Confirm the Board's minuted conclusion is consistent with the dashboard's adequacy status.
Log any mismatch between the minuted conclusion and the underlying dashboard as an exception.
testing.done: the capital/liquidity review minuted at each sampled Board meeting reconciles to the underlying dashboard.

testing.step: Trace director/committee change notifications to OSFI submission confirmations
actions: For every director or committee change in the sample period, pull the OSFI Changes in Corporate Information submission confirmation.
Compare the submission date to the change's effective date and confirm it falls within the prescribed notification window.
Log any late or missing notification as an exception.
testing.done: every sampled director/committee change traces to a timely OSFI submission confirmation.

testing.step: Test charter version control and Board approval evidence
actions: For each sampled charter version, confirm a dated Board resolution approving it exists in the board portal.
Confirm the superseded version is archived, not deleted, with a retirement date.
Log any charter version lacking a traceable approval resolution as an exception.
testing.done: every sampled charter version has a traceable, dated Board approval and an archived prior version.

testing.step: Log every exception with root cause, owner and remediation date
actions: Raise a GRC issue per exception with the meeting/charter identifier and the specific gap.
Assign root cause and owner, and set a remediation date.
Carry any open exception into the next quarter's test as a mandatory retest item.
testing.done: every exception has an issue, root cause, owner, remediation date and retest commitment.

testing.step: Conclude, sign and report the test
actions: Compute the exception rate against the zero-tolerance threshold for quorum and unapproved charter changes.
Write the conclusion (effective / effective with exceptions / ineffective) with evidence references.
Have an independent reviewer who authored none of the sampled work sign the workpaper.
Report the result to the Audit Committee at its next sitting and file the workpaper in the evidence repository.
testing.done: a signed workpaper with a stated conclusion and exception rate is reported to the Audit Committee and filed.

checklist.step: Open the annual governance disclosure file and set the AGM-minus-21-day deadline
actions: In the board portal, open a new Governance Disclosure workspace for the fiscal year and enter the AGM date.
Calculate the 21-day-before-AGM filing deadline and load it into the governance calendar with T-35/T-21 alerts.

List the required disclosure package contents: board/committee structure summary, director independence attestations, related-party transaction summary, and the Appointed Actuary's annual report status.
Assign a section owner for each content item.
checklist.done: the disclosure workspace exists with the AGM-minus-21-day deadline loaded and every section owned.

checklist.step: Request the Appointed Actuary's confirmation of any material-matters report status
actions: Email the Appointed Actuary requesting written confirmation of whether any matter was reported to the CEO/CFO under s. 369 during the year.
If a report was raised, request its resolution status: rectified, or escalated to directors, or escalated to OSFI.
File the actuary's written confirmation in the disclosure workspace regardless of answer.
checklist.done: a written confirmation from the Appointed Actuary on s. 369 report status for the year is on file.

checklist.step: Where a material-matters report was raised, verify it reached the CEO and CFO
actions: Pull the dated memo or email that first raised the matter with the CEO and CFO.
Confirm the memo states the matter, the financial-condition impact, and the rectification requested.
Attach the CEO/CFO's dated acknowledgement to the file.
checklist.done: the s. 369 report to the CEO/CFO is on file with a dated acknowledgement of receipt.

checklist.step: Escalate to directors and OSFI if the matter was not addressed
actions: If the CEO/CFO did not rectify the matter within the timeframe agreed, prepare a report to the Board setting out the matter, prior notice given, and the continuing risk.
Present the report at the next Board or Audit Committee meeting and have it minuted.
If the Board does not resolve it, submit a written report to OSFI's Office of the Superintendent naming the matter and the steps already taken.
File the OSFI submission confirmation with General Counsel.
checklist.done: any unresolved material matter is on the Board's minutes and, if still unresolved, reported to OSFI with a filed confirmation.

checklist.step: Assemble the board/committee structure and director independence sections
actions: Pull the current committee charter list and director independence attestations from the board portal.
Summarize each committee's mandate and current membership for the disclosure package.
Confirm director independence attestations are dated within the fiscal year.
checklist.done: the governance structure section is drafted from current, dated board portal records.

checklist.step: Assemble the related-party transaction summary section
actions: Pull the year's Conduct Review Committee-approved related-party transaction log.
Summarize transaction type, counterparty relationship, and committee approval date for each entry.
Confirm every logged transaction has a Conduct Review Committee approval on file before including it.
checklist.done: the related-party transaction section lists only committee-approved transactions with approval dates.

checklist.step: Draft the CGAD-equivalent governance disclosure narrative
actions: Combine the structure, independence, related-party and actuary-report sections into the annual governance disclosure narrative.
Cross-reference each factual statement to its source document in the workspace.
Send the draft to General Counsel and the CFO for content review.
checklist.done: a complete draft narrative with source cross-references is ready for legal and CFO review.

checklist.step: Obtain legal and CFO review of the draft disclosure
actions: Review the draft for completeness against s. 369/368 reporting requirements and OSFI governance disclosure expectations.
Confirm with the CFO that the financial-condition narrative matches the audited/interim financial statements.
Return mark-ups to the Corporate Secretary within 5 business days.
checklist.done: the draft carries General Counsel and CFO review comments or a clean sign-off, dated at least 10 business days before the AGM.

checklist.step: Table the disclosure package for Board approval
actions: Include the finalized disclosure package as a Board resolution item at the meeting held before the 21-day AGM deadline.
Record the Board's approval vote and any conditions in the minutes.
Publish the approved package in the board portal.
checklist.done: the Board's dated approval of the disclosure package is minuted before the 21-day deadline.

checklist.step: File the disclosure package through the Internal Regulatory System
actions: In the Internal Regulatory System, open the annual governance disclosure filing module and upload the approved package.
Complete the filer attestation fields and submit before the 21-day-before-AGM deadline.
Download and file the submission confirmation number.
checklist.done: the disclosure package is submitted with a confirmation number captured, on or before the 21-day deadline.

checklist.step: Publish the disclosure to shareholders/policyholders as required
actions: Post the approved governance disclosure summary to the investor/policyholder-facing section of the company website.
Include the disclosure package reference in the AGM notice materials.
Confirm the posting date is on or before the AGM.
checklist.done: the disclosure is publicly posted with the posting date on or before the AGM.

checklist.step: Track and escalate any missed section deadline
actions: Monitor the section-owner tracker weekly during the disclosure cycle.
Raise a GRC issue for any section owner missing their internal milestone.
Escalate to General Counsel if a miss threatens the 21-day filing deadline.
checklist.done: no section misses its milestone without a logged, escalated GRC issue.

checklist.step: Log any late filing or delayed actuary escalation as a compliance exception
actions: Raise an exception for any disclosure package filed after the 21-day deadline or any actuary report not escalated within its expected timeframe.
Assign root cause and owner and set a remediation date.
Notify the Chief Compliance Officer of any actuary-escalation exception the same day it is identified.
checklist.done: every late filing or delayed escalation has a logged exception with root cause, owner and remediation date.

checklist.step: Obtain General Counsel sign-off closing the annual cycle
actions: Confirm the filing confirmation number, publication evidence, and any exception remediation are all on file.
Sign and date the cycle-close record.
Notify the Corporate Secretary the cycle is closed.
checklist.done: the annual disclosure cycle carries a dated General Counsel sign-off with all evidence attached.

checklist.step: Retain the disclosure package and actuary escalation trail
actions: Move the final package, review comments, Board minutes, and any actuary escalation correspondence into the compliance evidence repository.
Apply the 7-year retention label under the fiscal year and AGM date.
Confirm the repository entry is indexed and searchable by fiscal year.
checklist.done: the complete disclosure cycle record is retained, labelled and searchable.

testing.step: Build the population of governance disclosures and actuary escalations in scope
actions: Pull every annual governance disclosure filed, and every s. 369 material-matters report raised, in the test period from the Internal Regulatory System and board minutes.
Reconcile the count of disclosures to the number of fiscal years/AGMs in scope.
Resolve any gap before sampling.
testing.done: the population is reconciled to the AGM calendar and signed as complete.

testing.step: Reconcile each disclosure package to a Board approval and filing confirmation
actions: Match each disclosure package to its Board approval minute and Internal Regulatory System confirmation number.
Check the filing date is on or before 21 days before the AGM.
List unmatched or late packages as automatic exceptions.
testing.done: every disclosure package is matched to a Board approval and a timely filing confirmation, or listed as an exception.

testing.step: Select the sample and document the selection method
actions: Take 100% of years with a s. 369 material-matters report raised.
Take all remaining annual disclosure packages in the test period (typically 1-3 years) given the low annual volume.
Record the population and selection basis in the workpaper.
testing.done: the sample covers every year with an actuary escalation and every disclosure package in the test period.

testing.step: Re-perform the CEO/CFO escalation check for each sampled actuary report
actions: Independently pull the dated memo raising the matter and the CEO/CFO's acknowledgement.
Confirm the memo date is contemporaneous with when the actuary identified the matter, not backdated.
Log any gap between identification and CEO/CFO notification as an exception.
testing.done: each sampled actuary report has an independently verified, timely CEO/CFO notification or a logged exception.

testing.step: Verify unresolved matters reached the Board and, where needed, OSFI
actions: For any sampled matter not rectified by the CEO/CFO, confirm it appears in Board or Audit Committee minutes.
Where the Board also did not resolve it, confirm an OSFI submission confirmation exists with a matching subject and date.
Log any matter that stalled without reaching directors or OSFI as a reportable exception, not a documentation gap.
testing.done: every unresolved sampled matter traces to Board minutes and, if still unresolved, an OSFI filing confirmation.

testing.step: Test the related-party transaction section against Conduct Review Committee approvals
actions: Trace each disclosed related-party transaction to its Conduct Review Committee approval minute.
Confirm the approval date pre-dates the transaction date.
Log any disclosed transaction lacking a pre-dated committee approval as an exception.
testing.done: every disclosed related-party transaction traces to a pre-dated Conduct Review Committee approval.

testing.step: Verify public posting and AGM-notice inclusion
actions: Check the investor/policyholder-facing website for the posted disclosure summary and capture the posting date.
Confirm the AGM notice materials reference the disclosure package.
Log a missing or late posting as an exception.
testing.done: the public posting date and AGM-notice reference are verified for every sampled year.

testing.step: Recompute the 21-day filing deadline for each sampled package
actions: Take the AGM date from the corporate calendar and subtract 21 days to compute the required filing deadline.
Compare to the actual Internal Regulatory System submission timestamp.
Log any package filed after the recomputed deadline as an exception.
testing.done: the recomputed deadline is compared to the actual filing timestamp for every sampled package with no unexplained lateness.

testing.step: Log every exception with root cause, owner and remediation date
actions: Raise a GRC issue per exception naming the fiscal year and the specific gap.
Assign root cause and owner and set a remediation date.
Carry open exceptions into next year's test as a mandatory retest item.
testing.done: every exception has an issue, root cause, owner, remediation date and retest commitment.

testing.step: Conclude, sign and report the test
actions: Compute the exception rate against the zero-tolerance threshold for missed escalations.
Write the conclusion with evidence references and any reportable breach flagged separately.
Have the independent reviewer sign the workpaper.
Report the result to the Audit Committee and file the workpaper in the evidence repository.
testing.done: a signed workpaper with a stated conclusion is reported to the Audit Committee and filed.

checklist.step: Open a fitness-and-propriety assessment file on nomination

Notify General Counsel and the Nominating Committee Chair that the file is open.
checklist.done: an HRIS appointment file exists for the nominee with the confirmation-blocking workflow active.

checklist.step: Run the background and credit/regulatory check

checklist.step: Test ICA director-composition eligibility

Document the composition-impact calculation showing before/after counts.
Reject or condition the appointment if it would breach the composition requirement, and notify the Nominating Committee Chair.
checklist.done: a documented before/after composition calculation confirms the appointment keeps the Board within ICA composition rules.

checklist.step: Collect conflict-of-interest and outside-directorship declarations
actions: Send the nominee the standard conflict-of-interest and outside-directorship disclosure form.
Review disclosed outside directorships for competitive or related-party conflicts.
Route any disclosed conflict to General Counsel for a written mitigation plan before appointment.
File the signed declaration in the HRIS record.
checklist.done: a signed conflict declaration is on file and any disclosed conflict has a written mitigation plan.

checklist.step: Confirm the nominee's competency and experience against the role profile
actions: Compare the nominee's CV and professional credentials against the Board/committee skills matrix gap the appointment is meant to fill.
Obtain two professional references and record the reference-check notes.
Attach the skills-matrix comparison to the file.
checklist.done: a documented skills-matrix comparison and two reference checks are on file.

checklist.step: For actuarial or finance-facing appointments, confirm support for the Appointed Actuary's s. 366 access rights
actions: Brief the nominee, as part of onboarding, on the statutory duty to grant the Appointed Actuary unfettered access to records, information and explanations under s. 366.
Obtain the nominee's written acknowledgement of this duty where the role has custody of records the actuary may need.
File the acknowledgement with the appointment record.
checklist.done: a written s. 366 access acknowledgement is on file for every appointee whose role controls records the actuary may need.

checklist.step: Obtain committee/Board approval of the appointment
actions: Table the completed assessment file as a Nominating Committee, then Board, approval item.
Record the approval vote and effective date in the board portal minutes.
Notify HR to proceed with formal appointment paperwork only after the Board vote is recorded.
checklist.done: a minuted Board approval with effective date exists before formal appointment paperwork proceeds.

checklist.step: Provision system and record access appropriate to the role
actions: In the IAM platform, create the access request tied to the approved role profile (board portal, financial systems, actuarial data as applicable).
Apply least-privilege access and route any access affecting actuarial data records through the Appointed Actuary for sign-off.
Confirm provisioning is complete before the appointee's start date.
checklist.done: role-appropriate access is provisioned and confirmed before the start date, with actuarial-data access signed off by the Appointed Actuary.

checklist.step: File the OSFI appointment notification
actions: Complete OSFI's Changes in Corporate Information return for the new director/officer with biography and fit-and-proper attestation attached.
Submit within the prescribed period after the appointment's effective date.
File the submission confirmation with the HRIS record.
checklist.done: the OSFI appointment notification is filed on time with a confirmation on record.

checklist.step: Close and lock the assessment file
actions: Mark every workflow step complete in the HRIS and release the appointment-confirmation block.
Have HR leadership countersign the completed file.
Lock the file from further edits except by authorized compliance review.
checklist.done: the HRIS file shows every step complete, countersigned, and locked.

checklist.step: Set the periodic re-assessment trigger for continuing directors/officers
actions: Schedule a renewed background and composition-eligibility check on each re-election or contract renewal date.
Load the trigger into the HRIS to auto-open a new assessment file 60 days before the renewal date.
Notify General Counsel when a re-assessment opens.
checklist.done: every continuing appointee has a scheduled re-assessment trigger tied to their re-election/renewal date.

checklist.step: Monitor for post-appointment adverse events
actions: Subscribe to a regulatory/sanctions watch-list alert service covering all current directors and officers.
Investigate any adverse alert within 5 business days and determine whether it affects continued eligibility.
Document the outcome in the individual's HRIS file.
checklist.done: an adverse-event monitoring subscription is active and every alert has a documented, timely investigation outcome.

checklist.step: Log incomplete or late assessments as exceptions
actions: Raise a GRC issue for any appointment confirmed before the assessment file was complete.
Assign root cause and owner and set a remediation date.
Escalate any resulting composition breach to General Counsel immediately.
checklist.done: every incomplete assessment or composition breach has a logged exception with owner and remediation date.

checklist.step: Obtain General Counsel sign-off on remediation
actions: Review the remediation evidence for the logged exception.
Sign and date the remediation close-out.
Notify HR and the Corporate Secretary the exception is closed.
checklist.done: every remediation closes with a dated General Counsel sign-off.

checklist.step: Retain the assessment file for tenure plus 7 years
actions: Move the locked assessment file into the compliance evidence repository under the individual's name and role.
Apply the tenure-plus-7-years retention label.
Confirm the file is retrievable by name for an OSFI inquiry.
checklist.done: the assessment file is retained, labelled, and retrievable by individual name.

testing.step: Build the population of director/officer appointments in the period
actions: Extract from the HRIS every director and senior officer appointment, re-election and renewal in the test period.
Reconcile the extract to the Board's minuted approval list for the same period.
Resolve any discrepancy before sampling.
testing.done: the population is reconciled to Board minutes and signed as complete.

testing.step: Reconcile every appointment to a completed assessment file
actions: Match each population row to a locked HRIS assessment file.
Check the file's completion date pre-dates the Board approval date.
List unmatched or late-completed files as automatic exceptions.
testing.done: every appointment is matched to a pre-dated, complete assessment file, or listed as an exception.

testing.step: Select the sample and document the selection method
actions: Take 100% of new (first-time) director and officer appointments in the period.
Take a random sample of half the re-elections/renewals, minimum 5.
Record the seed, population size and selection date in the workpaper.
testing.done: the sample covers every new appointment and a documented sample of renewals.

testing.step: Re-perform the composition-eligibility calculation for each sampled appointment
actions: Independently recompute the Canadian-residency and independence counts before and after the appointment using the roster as of the appointment date.
Compare to General Counsel's documented calculation; log any difference as an exception.
Capture the roster snapshot into the workpaper.
testing.done: each sampled appointment has an independently recomputed composition result reconciled to the documented one.

testing.step: Verify the background and regulatory-sanctions check on the sample
actions: Confirm a background-check report exists in the HRIS file for each sampled appointee, dated before appointment.
Spot-check the sanctions/regulatory-watch-list check independently against a public sanctions database for 3 sampled individuals.
Log any missing or contradicted result as an exception.
testing.done: each sampled appointee has a verified, pre-dated background check with no unresolved contradiction.

testing.step: Test conflict-of-interest declarations and mitigation plans
actions: Pull the signed conflict declaration for each sampled appointee.
For any disclosed conflict, confirm a written mitigation plan is on file and was actioned.
Log an undisclosed conflict discovered through public-record checks as an exception.
testing.done: every sampled appointee has a signed declaration and any disclosed conflict has a verified mitigation plan.

testing.step: Verify the s. 366 access acknowledgement for records-facing appointees
actions: Identify sampled appointees whose role controls records the actuary may need.
Confirm a written s. 366 acknowledgement is on file for each.
Confirm, from the actuary's own access log, that no information request to that individual was refused or delayed during the period.
testing.done: records-facing sampled appointees have a filed s. 366 acknowledgement and no logged access refusal.

testing.step: Trace the OSFI appointment notification for each sampled appointee
actions: In the Internal Regulatory System, pull the Changes in Corporate Information submission for each sampled appointee.
Compare the submission date to the appointment's effective date and confirm it is within the prescribed period.
Log any late or missing notification as an exception.
testing.done: every sampled appointment traces to a timely OSFI notification confirmation.

testing.step: Log every exception with root cause, owner and remediation date
actions: Raise a GRC issue per exception naming the appointee and the specific gap.
Assign root cause and owner and set a remediation date.
Carry open exceptions into the next test cycle as a mandatory retest item.
testing.done: every exception has an issue, root cause, owner, remediation date and retest commitment.

testing.step: Conclude, sign and report the test
actions: Compute the exception rate against the zero-tolerance threshold.
Write the conclusion with evidence references, flagging any composition breach as a reportable item.
Have the independent reviewer sign the workpaper.
Report the result to the Audit Committee and file the workpaper in the evidence repository.
testing.done: a signed workpaper with a stated conclusion is reported to the Audit Committee and filed.

checklist.step: Inventory governance policies due for annual review
actions: In the board portal policy library, pull every policy with a last-approval date 11 months or older.
Confirm the Related-Party Transaction Policy and the Investment & Lending Policy (s. 492) are on the list every year without exception.
Assign a policy owner for each item and set the review target date at least 30 days before the 12-month anniversary.
Notify each owner via the board portal workflow.
checklist.done: every policy due within the year is listed with an owner and a review target date.

checklist.step: Redline the Related-Party Transaction Policy against current ICA sections
actions: Compare the policy's permitted-transaction categories and approval thresholds to ss. 522-528.
Update any definition or threshold that has drifted from the statutory text.
Confirm the policy assigns the Conduct Review Committee as the approving body per s. 204.
Send the redline to the Conduct Review Committee Chair for review.
checklist.done: the redlined policy matches current ss. 522-528 categories/thresholds and names the Conduct Review Committee as approver.

checklist.step: Redline the Investment & Lending Policy against s. 492
actions: Compare the policy's asset-class limits and lending authority levels to s. 492 and the Investment Limits Regulations.
Update any limit or authority level that has changed since the last approval.
Confirm the policy names the committee responsible for ongoing limits monitoring.
Send the redline to General Counsel for a legal-sufficiency check.
checklist.done: the redlined Investment & Lending Policy matches current s. 492 limits and names a monitoring committee.

checklist.step: Collect the year's related-party transaction log for Conduct Review Committee review
actions: Pull every transaction logged as related-party in the year from the board portal.
For each, record the counterparty relationship, transaction type, and proposed terms.
Attach the market-comparable terms analysis prepared by Finance for each transaction.
Distribute the complete log to the Conduct Review Committee ahead of its meeting.
checklist.done: the year's complete related-party transaction log, with market-comparable analysis, is distributed to the committee.

checklist.step: Have the Conduct Review Committee determine each related-party transaction
actions: At the committee meeting, review each transaction against the permitted-transaction categories in ss. 522-528.
Confirm the proposed terms are at least as favourable to the company as a market transaction, using the Finance comparable analysis.
Record the committee's approval, rejection, or conditional approval for each transaction in the minutes.
File the signed determination against the transaction log entry.
checklist.done: every logged related-party transaction carries a minuted committee determination on market-comparability.

checklist.step: Confirm no related-party transaction was executed ahead of committee approval
actions: Compare the execution date on each transaction contract or agreement to the committee approval date.
Flag any transaction executed before its approval date to General Counsel the same day.
Record the flag in the transaction log entry pending remediation.
checklist.done: every transaction's execution date is confirmed on or after its committee approval date, or flagged.

checklist.step: Obtain Board approval of the redlined policies
actions: Table the Related-Party Transaction Policy and Investment & Lending Policy redlines as Board resolution items.
Record the Board's approval vote and effective date for each policy.
Publish the newly approved versions in the board portal policy library.
checklist.done: both policies carry a dated Board approval resolution and are published in the policy library.

checklist.step: Review and approve remaining governance policies on the annual list
actions: Confirm each remaining policy owner has submitted a redline or a 'no change needed' attestation.
Route each policy through its designated approving body (Board or relevant committee) per its charter.
Record approval votes and effective dates in the board portal.
checklist.done: every policy on the annual list carries a dated approval or a documented 'no change needed' attestation.

checklist.step: Publish approved policies and retire superseded versions
actions: Upload each newly approved policy version to the board portal policy library with its effective date.
Archive the superseded version with a retirement date and cross-reference to the new version.
Notify all policy stakeholders (Compliance, Risk, Finance) of the new effective dates.
checklist.done: every policy library entry shows the current version and an archived prior version with dates.

checklist.step: Distribute the updated policies to affected teams and confirm acknowledgement
actions: Send the updated Related-Party Transaction Policy and Investment & Lending Policy to Finance, Treasury and Investment teams.
Require an electronic acknowledgement of receipt and understanding from each named recipient.
Chase outstanding acknowledgements weekly until 100% complete.
checklist.done: 100% of named recipients have acknowledged the updated policies.

checklist.step: Update the related-party transaction pre-approval workflow to reflect any threshold change
actions: Update the Finance intake form's approval routing if the policy's transaction thresholds changed.
Test the updated workflow with a sample dummy transaction to confirm it routes to the Conduct Review Committee.
Notify Finance staff of the effective date of the updated workflow.
checklist.done: the intake workflow reflects the current policy thresholds and has been tested before go-live.

checklist.step: Brief the Investment Committee on the updated Investment & Lending Policy limits
actions: Present the newly approved Investment & Lending Policy limits at the next Investment Committee meeting, highlighting any change from the prior version.
Confirm the quarterly limits monitoring report template is updated to reference the new limit values.
Obtain the committee's acknowledgement, minuted, that the updated limits are now in effect for monitoring purposes.
Notify Investment Operations of the effective date for the new limits.
checklist.done: the Investment Committee has minuted acknowledgement of the updated limits and the monitoring report template reflects them.

checklist.step: Log any lapsed policy or unapproved transaction as an exception
actions: Raise a GRC issue for any policy that passed its 12-month anniversary without re-approval, or any transaction executed ahead of committee approval.
Assign root cause and owner and set a remediation date.
Escalate any executed-without-approval transaction to General Counsel immediately.
checklist.done: every lapsed policy or unapproved transaction has a logged exception with owner and remediation date.

checklist.step: Obtain General Counsel sign-off on remediation
actions: Review the remediation evidence for each logged exception.
Sign and date the remediation close-out, including any retroactive committee ratification obtained.
Notify the Board Governance Lead the exception is closed.
checklist.done: every remediation, including any retroactive ratification, closes with a dated General Counsel sign-off.

checklist.step: Retain the policy versions and transaction determinations
actions: Move approved policy versions, redlines, Board minutes and transaction determinations into the compliance evidence repository.
Apply the 7-year retention label; mark current policy versions for permanent retention.
Confirm the repository index is searchable by policy name and transaction counterparty.
checklist.done: the year's governance-policy and related-party transaction record is retained, labelled and searchable.

testing.step: Build the population of policy reviews and related-party transactions in the period
actions: Extract from the board portal every policy due for review and every related-party transaction logged in the test year.
Reconcile the transaction count to the Finance related-party transaction sub-ledger.
Resolve any discrepancy before sampling.
testing.done: the population is reconciled to the Finance sub-ledger and signed as complete.

testing.step: Reconcile every policy to a current approval and every transaction to a committee determination
actions: Match each policy to an approval dated within the prior 12 months.
Match each related-party transaction to a Conduct Review Committee determination.
List any policy past its anniversary, or transaction without a determination, as an automatic exception.
testing.done: every policy and transaction is matched to current evidence, or listed as an exception.

testing.step: Select the sample and document the selection method
actions: Take 100% of related-party transactions above the policy's materiality threshold.
Take a random sample of remaining transactions and policies, minimum 10 items combined, seeded and reproducible.
Record the seed, population size and selection date in the workpaper.
testing.done: the sample covers every material transaction and a documented random sample of the rest.

testing.step: Re-perform the market-comparability test for each sampled transaction
actions: Independently source market comparables for the transaction type (loan rate, lease rate, service fee benchmark) from an external pricing source.
Compare the transaction's actual terms to the independently sourced comparable.
Log any transaction priced less favourably to the company than the market comparable as an exception.
testing.done: each sampled transaction has an independent market-comparability re-performance recorded and reconciled.

testing.step: Verify the Conduct Review Committee's approval preceded execution
actions: Compare the committee's minuted approval date to the transaction contract's execution/signature date.
Log any transaction executed on or before the approval date (other than the approval date itself) as an exception.
Capture the minute excerpt and the contract signature page into the workpaper.
testing.done: every sampled transaction's execution date is verified against the approval date with any breach logged.

testing.step: Recompute the s. 492 investment/lending limits referenced in the policy
actions: Pull the underlying investment ledger balances used to set the policy's asset-class limits.
Recompute the ratios and compare to the limits stated in the newly approved Investment & Lending Policy.
Log any limit in the policy that does not match the current Investment Limits Regulations as an exception.
testing.done: the policy's stated limits are independently recomputed and reconciled to the regulation and the ledger.

testing.step: Test policy version control and distribution acknowledgement
actions: Confirm each sampled policy's current version has a dated Board approval and an archived prior version.
Check the distribution log for 100% recipient acknowledgement of the updated policy.
Log any missing acknowledgement or broken version history as an exception.
testing.done: version control and distribution acknowledgement are verified for every sampled policy.

testing.step: Confirm the intake workflow enforces the updated approval thresholds
actions: Submit a test transaction through the Finance intake workflow at a value just above the policy threshold.
Confirm it routes to the Conduct Review Committee and cannot be approved by Finance alone.
Log a workflow that fails to enforce the threshold as a control-design exception.
testing.done: the intake workflow is independently confirmed to enforce the current policy threshold.

testing.step: Log every exception with root cause, owner and remediation date
actions: Raise a GRC issue per exception naming the policy or transaction and the specific gap.
Assign root cause and owner and set a remediation date.
Carry open exceptions into the next annual test as a mandatory retest item.
testing.done: every exception has an issue, root cause, owner, remediation date and retest commitment.

testing.step: Conclude, sign and report the test
actions: Compute the exception rate against the zero-tolerance threshold for unapproved transactions.
Write the conclusion with evidence references, flagging any unapproved transaction as a reportable item.
Have the independent reviewer sign the workpaper.
Report the result to the Audit Committee and file the workpaper in the evidence repository.
testing.done: a signed workpaper with a stated conclusion is reported to the Audit Committee and filed.

checklist.step: Open the year-end statutory close calendar
actions: In the close/consolidation tool, load the year-end close calendar with the OSFI annual-return deadline and, for US-licensed business, the March 1 NAIC deadline.
Assign task owners for trial balance close, statutory adjustments, schedule preparation and disclosure drafting.
Set T-30/T-15/T-5 milestone alerts against each filing deadline.
Distribute the calendar to Finance, Actuarial and the external Auditor.
checklist.done: the close calendar with all statutory deadlines and task owners is loaded and distributed.

checklist.step: Close the general ledger and produce the statutory trial balance
actions: Run the period-end close routine in the ERP, posting all accrual, reinsurance and intercompany entries.
Extract the statutory trial balance and reconcile total assets/liabilities to the prior period plus current-period movements.
Resolve any unreconciled variance above the 0.5%-of-total-assets threshold before proceeding.
Lock the ledger period once reconciled.
checklist.done: the statutory trial balance is closed, reconciled within threshold, and the ledger period is locked.

checklist.step: Apply statutory accounting adjustments to convert from GAAP to the prescribed statutory basis
actions: Identify every GAAP-to-statutory adjustment required (non-admitted assets, statutory reserve basis, deferred acquisition cost treatment).
Post each adjustment with a documented rationale and the ICA/OSFI guideline reference supporting it.
Route adjustments above a materiality threshold to the CFO for review before posting.
Retain the adjustment workpaper set for audit.
checklist.done: every GAAP-to-statutory adjustment is posted with a documented rationale and CFO review where material.

checklist.step: Build the investment schedule demonstrating ss. 492-495 compliance
actions: Pull the year-end investment portfolio detail and classify each holding by asset class (real property, equity, commercial loan, fixed income).
Compute each asset class's ratio to total assets and compare to the Investment Limits (Insurance Companies) Regulations thresholds.
Flag any asset class approaching or exceeding its limit to the Chief Risk Officer.
Attach the completed schedule to the statutory statement package.
checklist.done: the investment schedule is built, limit ratios computed, and any threshold issue flagged before the package is finalized.

checklist.step: Prepare the appointed actuary's reserve figures for inclusion in the statements
actions: Run the year-end policy liability valuation in the actuarial modeling platform for all in-force business.
Reconcile the resulting reserve figures to the prior year's roll-forward plus current-year experience.
Deliver the certified reserve figures and the actuarial valuation report to the Controller for statement inclusion.
Retain the model run log and assumption set supporting the figures.
checklist.done: certified reserve figures and the valuation report are delivered to the Controller with a retained model run log.

checklist.step: Draft the financial statements per the OSFI prescribed annual return format
actions: In the Internal Regulatory System, open the annual return template for the current filing year.
Populate the balance sheet, statement of income, and required exhibits from the closed trial balance, adjustments and reserve figures.
Run the template's built-in tie-out checks (balance sheet balances, exhibit cross-foots).
Resolve every tie-out failure before moving to review.
checklist.done: the annual return is populated in the Internal Regulatory System with all built-in tie-out checks passing.

checklist.step: Prepare NAIC Annual Statement blanks for US-licensed business, if applicable
actions: In the Statutory Reporting (NAIC) system, populate the applicable Annual Statement blank (Life, Health or P&C) for the US-licensed entity.
Map the OSFI-basis figures to the NAIC statutory accounting basis, documenting every basis difference.
Run the NAIC blank's edit checks and resolve every failed edit.
Confirm the blank ties to the domiciliary-state filing requirements.
checklist.done: the NAIC Annual Statement blank passes all edit checks and every OSFI-to-NAIC basis difference is documented.

checklist.step: Complete the disclosure checklist
actions: Work through the annual disclosure checklist covering related-party transactions, subsequent events, and investment concentration disclosures.
Confirm each disclosure ties to a source document (Conduct Review Committee log, investment schedule).
Flag any disclosure item lacking source support to General Counsel.
checklist.done: every disclosure checklist item is completed and tied to a source document, or flagged.

checklist.step: Route the draft statements for CFO and Appointed Actuary review
actions: Send the complete draft package to the CFO and the Appointed Actuary for review.
Track review comments and resolve each before the package moves to the external Auditor.
Record sign-off from both reviewers with date and version number.
checklist.done: the CFO and Appointed Actuary sign off on the draft with all review comments resolved.

checklist.step: Coordinate the external Auditor's review of the statements
actions: Deliver the reviewed draft package and supporting workpapers to the external Auditor per the audit plan timeline.
Respond to auditor requests for additional evidence within 3 business days.
Incorporate any auditor-proposed adjustment and obtain the Auditor's clean or qualified opinion.
checklist.done: the external Auditor's opinion is obtained and any proposed adjustment is incorporated into the final package.

checklist.step: Obtain Board/Audit Committee approval of the final statements
actions: Table the final statements, including the Auditor's opinion, at the Audit Committee then full Board for approval.
Record the approval vote and date in the minutes.
Notify the filing team the statements are cleared to file.
checklist.done: a minuted Board approval of the final statements, with the Auditor's opinion attached, precedes filing.

checklist.step: File the statements with OSFI and, where applicable, the NAIC/state regulators
actions: Submit the approved annual return through the Internal Regulatory System before the OSFI deadline.
Submit the NAIC Annual Statement blank through the Statutory Reporting (NAIC) system by March 1 for US-licensed business.
Download and file both submission confirmations.
checklist.done: both filings are submitted before their respective deadlines with confirmations captured.

checklist.step: Log any missed close milestone or tie-out failure as an exception
actions: Raise a tracker issue for any close-calendar milestone missed by more than 2 business days.
Assign root cause and owner and set a remediation date.
Escalate any issue threatening the statutory filing deadline to the CFO immediately.
checklist.done: every missed milestone has a logged exception with owner and remediation date.

checklist.step: Obtain CFO sign-off closing the statutory close cycle
actions: Confirm both filing confirmations, the Auditor's opinion, and any exception remediation are on file.
Sign and date the cycle-close record.
Notify the Controller the cycle is closed.
checklist.done: the statutory close cycle carries a dated CFO sign-off with all evidence attached.

checklist.step: Retain the close workpapers and filed statements
actions: Move the trial balance, adjustment workpapers, investment schedule, disclosure checklist and filed statements into the compliance evidence repository.
Apply the 7-year retention label under the fiscal year.
Confirm the repository index is searchable by fiscal year and filing type.
checklist.done: the complete statutory close record is retained, labelled and searchable by fiscal year.

testing.step: Build the population of statutory statements filed in the period
actions: Pull every annual and quarterly statutory statement filed with OSFI (and NAIC blanks for US-licensed business) in the test period.
Reconcile the count to the close calendar's planned filing schedule.
Resolve any discrepancy before sampling.
testing.done: the population is reconciled to the close calendar and signed as complete.

testing.step: Reconcile each filed statement to the underlying trial balance
actions: Match total assets, liabilities and net income on each filed statement to the closed, locked trial balance for the same period.
Recompute the GAAP-to-statutory adjustments from the workpapers and confirm they tie to the filed figures.
List any unreconciled variance above 0.5% of total assets as an automatic exception.
testing.done: every filed statement reconciles to its trial balance and adjustment workpapers within threshold.

checklist.done: a planning memo with materiality, scope and a dated opinion-delivery timeline is circulated and loaded into the close tool.

checklist.step: Confirm auditor independence and finalize the engagement letter before fieldwork
actions: Obtain the external Auditor's written independence confirmation covering the audit firm and any affiliated non-audit services performed in the year.
Review the engagement letter for scope, fee, and reporting-line terms and confirm it names the Audit Committee as the party the Auditor reports to.
Route the engagement letter to the Audit Committee Chair for countersignature.
File the signed engagement letter and independence confirmation before fieldwork begins.
checklist.done: a signed engagement letter and independence confirmation are on file before audit fieldwork begins.

checklist.step: Build and track the prepared-by-client (PBC) evidence list
actions: Enter every PBC item the Auditor requests (trial balance, reconciliations, investment confirmations, related-party transaction log, reserve support) into a tracked list with a due date per item.
Assign an owner per PBC item across Finance, Actuarial and Investment Operations.
Update the list status weekly during the audit fieldwork window.
Escalate any PBC item more than 3 business days overdue to the Controller.
checklist.done: the PBC list is fully populated, owned and tracked, with overdue items escalated within 3 business days.

checklist.step: Coordinate the Appointed Actuary's liaison with the Auditor on reserve adequacy
actions: Provide the Auditor the certified actuarial valuation report and the assumption-change memo supporting the year's reserves.
Make the Appointed Actuary available for the Auditor's specialist review sessions on methodology and assumptions.
Respond to Auditor follow-up questions on the reserve calculation within 3 business days.
Log the Auditor's specialist-review sign-off on reserves once received.
checklist.done: the Auditor's specialist review of reserves is supported with the required actuarial evidence and a logged sign-off.

checklist.step: Confirm the Auditor considered the s. 369 material-matters position
actions: Provide the Auditor the Appointed Actuary's written confirmation of any s. 369 report raised during the year and its resolution status.
Request the Auditor's written acknowledgement that the matter (or its absence) was factored into the audit risk assessment.
File the Auditor's acknowledgement with the audit-coordination workpapers.
checklist.done: the Auditor's written acknowledgement that the s. 369 position was considered is on file.

checklist.step: Respond to audit findings and proposed adjustments
actions: Log every audit finding and proposed adjustment received from the Auditor with its dollar impact.
Research and respond to each finding within 5 business days, either agreeing and posting the adjustment or providing a documented rebuttal.
Route any disagreement the Auditor does not accept to the Audit Committee for resolution.
Track the finding to closure in the audit-coordination log.
checklist.done: every audit finding has a timely response, resolution, and closure entry in the log.

checklist.step: Obtain the signed management representation letter
actions: Review the Auditor's draft management representation letter for accuracy against the year's known events, including any s. 369 matter.
Obtain CEO and CFO signatures on the letter dated as of the opinion date.
Deliver the signed letter to the Auditor before the opinion is issued.
File a copy with the audit-coordination workpapers.
checklist.done: a signed, dated management representation letter is delivered to the Auditor before the opinion is issued.

checklist.step: Receive and review the Auditor's opinion
actions: Receive the draft opinion and confirm it covers the correct entity, period and statement basis (statutory basis for the OSFI filing).
Confirm the opinion type (unqualified, qualified, adverse, disclaimer) and, if not unqualified, brief the CFO and Audit Committee immediately.
Confirm the opinion is signed and dated by the Auditor.
Attach the final opinion to the statement package.
checklist.done: a signed, dated opinion of the correct type is attached to the statement package, with any non-unqualified opinion escalated immediately.

checklist.step: Table the audited statements and opinion for Audit Committee/Board approval
actions: Present the audited statements and the Auditor's opinion to the Audit Committee, then the full Board, for approval.
Have the Auditor attend to answer questions on the opinion and any findings.
Record the Board's approval vote and date in the minutes.
checklist.done: a minuted Board approval of the audited statements and opinion, with the Auditor present, precedes filing.

checklist.step: File the audited statements with OSFI
actions: Attach the signed opinion to the annual return package in the Internal Regulatory System.
Submit before the prescribed deadline after financial year-end.
Download and file the submission confirmation.
checklist.done: the audited statements with the signed opinion attached are filed before deadline with a confirmation on file.

checklist.step: Provide the audited statements to the external Auditor's engagement file requirements and any US NAIC filing
actions: For US-licensed business, attach the equivalent audited-financials opinion package to the NAIC filing per the state's audit-filing requirement (typically June 1).
Confirm the audit opinion basis (statutory) matches what the state accepts.
File the confirmation with the audit-coordination record.
checklist.done: the audited statements are provided to the NAIC filing where required, with a confirmation on file.

checklist.step: Close out unresolved audit findings after filing
actions: Confirm every logged audit finding shows a closure entry (adjustment posted or rebuttal accepted).
For findings that remain open past filing, document the remediation plan and target date.
Report any open finding to the Audit Committee at its next sitting.
checklist.done: every audit finding is closed or carries a documented remediation plan reported to the Audit Committee.

checklist.step: Log any PBC delay or coordination breakdown as an exception
actions: Raise a tracker issue for any PBC item delivered more than 3 business days late or any milestone missed against the planning-memo timeline.
Assign root cause and owner and set a remediation date.
Escalate to the CFO any delay that pushed the opinion date close to the filing deadline.
checklist.done: every coordination delay has a logged exception with owner and remediation date.

checklist.step: Obtain CFO sign-off closing the audit-coordination cycle
actions: Confirm the signed opinion, filing confirmation and finding closure log are all on file.
Sign and date the cycle-close record.
Notify the Controller and Audit Committee the cycle is closed.
checklist.done: the audit-coordination cycle carries a dated CFO sign-off with all evidence attached.

checklist.step: Retain the audit-coordination record
actions: Move the PBC list, evidence package, management representation letter, opinion and finding log into the compliance evidence repository under the fiscal year.
Apply the 7-year retention label.
Confirm the repository index is searchable by fiscal year and finding status.
checklist.done: the complete audit-coordination record is retained, labelled and searchable by fiscal year.

testing.step: Build the population of audit cycles and audited filings in the period
actions: Identify every annual audit cycle completed and every audited statement filing made in the test period.
Reconcile the count to the number of fiscal years in scope.
Resolve any gap before sampling.
testing.done: the population is reconciled to the fiscal years in scope and signed as complete.

testing.step: Reconcile each audited filing to a signed opinion covering the correct period
actions: Match each filed statement to its attached opinion and confirm the opinion's period and entity match the filing.
Confirm the opinion is signed and dated before the filing submission date.
List any filing with a missing, mismatched, or undated opinion as an automatic exception.
testing.done: every audited filing is matched to a correctly dated, signed opinion, or listed as an exception.

testing.step: Select the sample and document the selection method
actions: Take 100% of audit cycles in the test period given the low annual volume.
Within each cycle, sample 5 PBC items and 5 audit findings at random, seeded and reproducible.
Record the seed, population and selection date in the workpaper.
testing.done: every audit cycle is covered, with a documented random sample of PBC items and findings within each.

testing.step: Re-perform the PBC timeliness check
actions: For each sampled PBC item, compute the days between the Auditor's request date and the actual delivery date.
Compare to the 3-business-day escalation standard.
Log any item that breached the standard without a logged exception as a control-design failure.
testing.done: PBC timeliness is independently recomputed for the sample and reconciled to the escalation standard.

testing.step: Verify the Appointed Actuary's specialist-review support to the Auditor
actions: Confirm the Auditor's specialist-review sign-off on reserves exists for the sampled cycle.
Independently compare the certified valuation report provided to the Auditor against the figure actually filed on the balance sheet.
Log any mismatch between what was provided to the Auditor and what was filed as an exception.
testing.done: the actuarial support provided to the Auditor is verified as complete and consistent with the filed figures.

testing.step: Verify the s. 369 acknowledgement was obtained from the Auditor
actions: Pull the Auditor's written acknowledgement that the s. 369 material-matters position was considered.
Compare it to the Appointed Actuary's own confirmation of the year's s. 369 position.
Log any inconsistency or a missing acknowledgement as an exception.
testing.done: the Auditor's s. 369 acknowledgement is verified against the actuary's own record for the sampled cycle.

testing.step: Test resolution of sampled audit findings
actions: For each sampled finding, confirm the response (adjustment posted or rebuttal) is documented and dated within 5 business days of the finding.
Where an adjustment was posted, trace it into the general ledger and confirm it flows to the filed statement.
Log any finding lacking a timely, traceable resolution as an exception.
testing.done: each sampled finding's resolution is independently traced and confirmed timely.

testing.step: Verify the management representation letter predates the opinion
actions: Pull the signed management representation letter for the sampled cycle.
Compare its signature date to the opinion's issue date.
Log any letter dated on or after the opinion date as an exception.
testing.done: the management representation letter's date is independently confirmed to precede the opinion for each sampled cycle.

testing.step: Log every exception with root cause, owner and remediation date
actions: Raise a tracker issue per exception naming the audit cycle and the specific gap.
Assign root cause and owner and set a remediation date.
Carry open exceptions into next year's audit-coordination test as a mandatory retest item.
testing.done: every exception has an issue, root cause, owner, remediation date and retest commitment.

testing.step: Conclude, sign and report the test
actions: Compute the exception rate against the zero-tolerance threshold for a missing or mismatched opinion.
Write the conclusion with evidence references and flag any non-unqualified opinion or unresolved finding separately.
Have the independent reviewer sign the workpaper.
Report the result to the Audit Committee and file the workpaper in the evidence repository.
testing.done: a signed workpaper with a stated conclusion is reported to the Audit Committee and filed.
